newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher as financials slide.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher as financials slide.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals ended solidly higher Friday, as gold in particular benefited from the sharp slide in the U.S. dollar, U.S. treasury bonds and U.S. stocks.

"The gold market was looking for a reason to recover after seeing 12-year lows last month and the sell off in financial markets provided the impetus," Chase Manhattan managing director for global commodities, Dinsa Mehta, said.
"The weakness in the dollar was especially significant as the dollar's strength has been a factor in gold's weakness of late," Mehta he said.

The U.S. dollar fell heavily against yen and deutchemark and the dollar's trade weighted index ended down 1.26 percent at 99.76 points late Friday, after seeing a new seven year high at 101.79 points earlier this week.

"Gold is still only about $10.00 an ounce off its 12-year lows, but the bullion market has absorbed huge supply in recent weeks and there is a feeling that today could be the start of some asset price deflation, so my own feeling is gold could edge higher from here," he said.
COMEX Decembert gold ended up $4.60 an ounce at $330.40, after seeing a session high at $332.00, its highest level in a week. Estimated COMEX gold volume was a solid 48,000 lots.

"J. Aron (the commodities trading arm of Goldman Sachs) and the trade were the main buyers early, but as the stock market fell there was substantial buying and shortcovering by funds, especially on the break above $330.00," Pell Brothers COMEX floor trader, Don Tierney, said.

Earlier COMEX gold open interest had risen 3,787 lots Thursday to 202,103 contracts, suggesting funds were re-establishing short positions, after gold looked to be about to re-test its 12 year lows earlier this week.

"But the break of the Dow's uptrend line since April around 8,075 points in particular saw some very heavy paper coming into the gold ring, and when the stock market was making its lows for the day, gold was making it's highs," Tierney said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended down 156 points at 8031 points, after falling below the 8,000 level intraday.
The S&P500 index ended down 17.65 points at 933.54, after seeing a 31 percent gain since the 10 pct downward correction in the index in April this year.
U.S. treasury bonds ended sharply lower also, after the 30 year long bond this week failed to clearly breach resistance at last December's high around 116 points.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $326.90/40 an ounce, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $323.70 and the New York close around $321.70/20.

Gold equities benefitted from the rise in gold prices though, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's index of North American gold and silver mining stocks ending up 4.32 pct at 102.47 points, its highest level since mid-June.
COMEX September silver settled unchanged at $4.375 an ounce, after seeing a session high at $4.475, as silver recovered from a slide earlier this week from over $4.50.
COMEX September silver options expired Friday.
NYMEX platinum and palladium futures ended sharply higher Friday also, after correcting for three days from new contract highs.
NYMEX October platinum closed up $11.10 at $443.70 an ounce, while NYMEX September palladium ended up $11.75 at $224.25 an ounce.
Earlier Friday TOCOM platinum group metal (PGM) prices rose by the daily limit on another bout of shortcovering.
Private investor short positions in TOCOM palladium were said to be still large at around 30 tonnes, but had fallen from around 50 tonnes in July, traders said.
Earlier this week TOCOM PGM prices had corrected downward sharply, ahead of the arrival of the August consignment of Russian PGMs in Japan.

Under the annual supply contract with Japanese trade houses, Russian platinum and palladium were put on an Aeroflot jet Thursday for arrival in Japan Friday, according to reports quoting Yuri Zhigulov, the Japan representative of Russian metal export agency, Almaz. The shipments are expected to satisfy Russia's contract obligations for the month.

One month platinum lease rates remained around 20 pct, while one month palladium ingot lease rates were around 80 pct and one month palladium sponge lease rates were around 100 percent, refining sources said.
